title: Terraform logging gateway: CloudTrail -> OpenSearch with tiered retention and health probes
creator: Maya Patel
description: Goal: Provide a reusable Terraform module (tfmodule) that wires account-level CloudTrail -> centralized S3 -> OpenSearch ingest pipeline with configurable tiered retention (hot/warm/cold) and automated health probes. The module must be suitable for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments and support cross-account logging patterns, KMS encryption for S3 and snapshots, and safe migration for existing clusters. It must expose knobs for retention policies, ILM integration, daily snapshot cadence, and an automated health check that validates log delivery and index freshness.
acceptance_criteria: Module deploys in a customer VPC and creates (optionally) the S3 landing bucket, CloudTrail configuration, and OpenSearch ingest resources without manual changes
Configurable variables: retention_days, warm_transition_days, cold_transition_days, snapshot_bucket_arn, kms_key_id, cross_account_trail_role allow standard deployment patterns
OpenSearch ILM policies created and applied; indices automatically transition through hot/warm/cold according to variables
Daily snapshot to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket and lifecycle rule to transition snapshots to Glacier after configurable days
Health probe Lambda publishes a metric (Custom CloudWatch namespace) that signals: last successfully ingested object timestamp, index write latency, and failed ingest count
Alerting playbook: CloudWatch alarm on probe -> PagerDuty runbook link in module README
Existing clusters can opt into the new ILM via a migration mode; migration docs and a dry-run flag included
Module has unit tests (terratest) and an integration smoke test that runs in CI and a canary namespace in sandbox
Manual review and security signoff completed (KMS usage, IAM least privilege verified)
implementation_notes: Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Logging+Gateway+TFModule (internal) contains detailed diagrams and variable list
Terraform layout: modules/logging-gateway/ with submodules: s3-bucket, cloudtrail-config, os-ingest-policy, ilm-operator, snapshot-scheduler, health-probe
S3 bucket lifecycle: objects -> transition to INTELLIGENT_TIERING for logs, snapshots -> transition to GLACIER after snapshot_glacier_days variable
OpenSearch: use index templates with write alias; module will create ingest pipeline that normalizes CloudTrail records into a single index schema
ILM: default policy: hot (0-7d), warm (7-30d), cold (30-90d); fully configurable via var map

Health probe: small Lambda in customer account with permissions to query OpenSearch and check S3 prefixes; publishes CloudWatch metric 'redwood.logging.gateway.delivery' with tags {account, region, env}
IAM: cross-account role for central logging account limited to PutObject on target bucket + AssumeRole only from org-admin principals
KMS: require customer-managed KMS key id input; we will block deployment if kms_key_id is empty when enable_encryption=true
Snapshots: use Curator-like scheduler (Lambda + EventBridge) to create snapshots to snapshot_bucket_arn
Migration: migration_mode = "dry-run"|"apply" - dry-run writes to console and creates test indices only
Testing: terratest module unit tests (local), CI integration uses a dedicated sandbox AWS account and reuses existing ENG sandbox infra (referenced in PR)
risks_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoff: pushing ILM decisions into the module simplifies ops but may conflict with customers who already enforce index lifecycle centrally. We provide a migration_mode for safer adoption.
Risk: cross-account CloudTrail requires careful IAM scoping; overly permissive roles would violate security posture. Work with security to lock down AssumeRole principals.
Tradeoff: snapshot frequency vs. cost — default daily snapshots retained 30 days; customers with high retention requirements should pass snapshot lifecycle vars.
Operational cost: health probe introduces additional read/API cost for OpenSearch. We batch checks and run every 5m by default to limit cost.
Compatibility: module initially supports OpenSearch 1.x and 2.x API surfaces; some ILM APIs differ between versions. We will add a version var and limit automated changes to supported versions.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge module into terraform-modules repo behind feature flag (modules.logging_gateway.enabled)
2) Run CI integration tests in sandbox account -> upload test artifacts to artifacts.redwood.ai for auditing
3) Invite 2 pilot customers from enterprise cohort to opt into module with SRE assistance
4) Run migration_mode=dry-run against pilot clusters to surface ILM conflicts; capture changes in migration report
5) After validation, schedule a maintenance window and apply migration_mode=apply for pilot; validate index health and snapshot integrity for 48 hours
6) Document rollback steps: restore from latest snapshot if corruption or data loss suspected; snapshots are retained per snapshot_retention_days var
7) Post-rollout: create a dashboard in Console showing delivery lag, probe metrics, and snapshot success rate
testing_plan: Unit: terratest for each submodule (s3-bucket, cloudtrail-config, ilm-operator)
Integration: one-shot deploy in ENG sandbox account as part of PR pipeline (PR #412) https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules/pull/412
End-to-end: create CloudTrail events, verify S3 landing, run ingest Lambda, validate index write, verify ILM transitions after simulated dates
Canary: deploy to sandbox canary namespace with low retention to validate snapshot and restore procedure
Chaos: simulate OpenSearch node failure to validate snapshot + retention resilience (post-merge test run)
Security tests: run gov-checks and terraform-compliance to ensure IAM and KMS usage meet policy
